title: Trouble tickets are read from the logging tree, never asked over the bus
owner: CC builds it; cairn/devices/trouble owns the store and its read tool, and each caller (cairn device pane, web_server, counting_block, the trouble CLI) owns its switch to it
intention: Trouble tickets are read and cleared as file artifacts in the logging tree through a tool trouble publishes, so no trouble message ever travels the bus and the bus holds no rows for trouble tickets.
why: Akien 2026-10-18, verbatim: 'TROUBLE TICKETS ARE A FILE ARTIFACT IN THE LOGGING TREE' and 'THERE SHOULD BE NO ROWS FOR TROUBLE TICKETS'. Measured the same day: 195 bus rows on cairn's personal channel, each a ~325 KB copy of the open trouble list (the cairn device pane asking verb live on every render), and 372 counting_block 'clears' rows plus 24 CC 'clear' rows addressed to trouble. The 2 s newest-200 read nearly fails because of them (trouble live-newest-200-read-near-misses-its-2s-bound).
traces_to: Akien 2026-10-18, verbatim: 'TROUBLE TICKETS ARE A FILE ARTIFACT IN THE LOGGING TREE' and 'THERE SHOULD BE NO ROWS FOR TROUBLE TICKETS'; his 2026-10-11 ruling that trouble tickets are logging artifacts in .cairn/logs/cairn/troubletickets (ticket 4ddc9df3369e); Law 5 (the bus database is the working surface and carries what is needed now; the bus intention: the database exists to queue undelivered messages); RULE 1 (callers reach trouble only through its declared public_interface, which store.py already is).
how: Grow cairn/devices/trouble/store.py (already in trouble's public_interface, imports only the address door) with the three reads/writes its bus verbs serve today: live() (the summary rows _handle_live returns), clears(prefix) (the rows _handle_clears returns) and clear(...) (the same gate _handle_clear runs, the owner's code). Point the three bus callers at it: the cairn device's trouble pane (cairn/devices/cairn/device.py:134), web_server's websocket (cairn/devices/web_server/listener.py:78) and counting_block (cairn/machines/counting_block/block.py:288), plus every `cairn trouble clear` path that sends verb clear. Retire live, clear and clears from TroubleDevice.declared_verbs. Raise is already a tool (DiagnosticBase.raise_trouble writes one file) and is untouched. Deleting the rows already standing is a separate ticket that waits on this one PROVED. CALLERS (measured 2026-10-18): Census of every bus caller of trouble, by grep over cairn/, bin/ and skills/ excluding proofs (to="trouble", to='trouble', reach('trouble')): (1) cairn/devices/cairn/device.py:134 _trouble_pane_data, verb live; (2) cairn/devices/web_server/listener.py:78 _handle_ws_troubles, verb live; (3) cairn/machines/counting_block/block.py:288 _ask_clears, verb clears; (4) cairn/devices/trouble/0/bin/trouble `live` subcommand line 24, verb live; (5) same file `clear` subcommand line 79, verb clear; (6) same file `drain` calls reach('trouble') only to pulse the shim, which it then drains itself. Bus rows measured 2026-10-18 by RemoteBus().read: newest 400 to trouble = 372 counting_block clears, 24 CC clear, 2 cli live, 2 CC live; newest 200 to cairn = 195 trouble live replies averaging ~325 KB. Out of this ticket and named so they are not lost: deleting those standing rows (a sibling ticket, after this one is PROVED, per Akien 'those wrong and bad things all deleted once it's fixed'), and one-trouble-per-problem identity across the originators (a sibling ticket). ASSUMPTIONS: Three load-bearing assumptions, each measured or bound to a tooth. (a) Readers can read the store without folding pending emissions first: measured 2026-10-18 21:13 that drains run at raise time (TroubleShim.receive_raise, the poke) and on pulse (TroubleShim.on_pulse); ~/.cairn/devices/trouble/0/drained.json was last written 17:33:34, seconds after the last raise. So a store read lags only an emission whose raiser wired no notifier, until the next pulse. The builder does NOT call fold_pending from store.py (that imports trouble/shim.py and through base/shim.py the bus client, the 2026-10-13 sieve measurement store.py's docstring records). (b) cairn.devices.trouble.store is importable by other components under RULE 1: it is declared in trouble's charter public_interface ['cairn.devices.trouble.trouble', 'cairn.devices.trouble.store']; the build runs the inspector's encapsulation_holds and fire_path_unreachable over the three callers to measure it. (c) Clearing stays the owner's act under Law 6: the CLI writes the clear as an emission through DiagnosticBase.clear_trouble (the existing send half, diagnostic.py:391) and then folds it with trouble's own TroubleShim.drain, which the CLI already does for `cairn trouble drain`; the CLI lives at cairn/devices/trouble/0/bin/trouble, inside the trouble component, so it is the owner's own code.
falsifier: Falsifier: with scratch roots and no bus reachable (bus_client.reach patched to raise), the cairn pane handler, the web_server websocket payload builder, counting_block's clears read, and `cairn trouble live` / `clear` all still produce their output from a scratch trouble store; TroubleDevice.declared_verbs carries none of live, clear, clears; and a corpus scan of cairn/, bin/ and skills/ (proofs excluded) finds no request addressed to trouble. Red if any of those reaches the bus or any verb remains. Horizon: the proof seals green and the hollow revert of store.py, the three callers and trouble.py reds it.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> [FIXME:waiting] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> PROVED
watchme: none, because the outcome is structural and checked by the proof cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_trouble_never_rides_the_bus.py (its corpus tooth scans cairn/, bin/ and skills/ for any request addressed to trouble), and the live count of bus rows to or from trouble is measured to zero by the sibling deletion ticket that waits on this one PROVED, against the 372 + 24 + 4 + 195 rows measured 2026-10-18 and recorded in this cast's missing_check
builder_notes: Questions a Haiku builder would need, answered here. Q: what do the new store functions return? A: store.live(roots=None) returns, for each *.json at the TOP of store_root(roots) in sorted order, the dict {k: ticket.get(k) for k in trouble.LIVE_SUMMARY_KEYS}; an unreadable file returns {'id': stem, 'standing': 'OPEN', 'count': 1, 'why': 'UNREADABLE TROUBLE FILE: <exc>', 'unreadable': True}, exactly as TroubleDevice._listing does; move LIVE_SUMMARY_KEYS into store.py and have trouble.py re-export it. store.clears(prefix='', roots=None) returns exactly the rows _handle_clears returns today, over the top of the store plus cleared/ (CLEARED_DIR, also moved into store.py and re-exported). Q: can store.py import trouble.py? A: no; trouble.py imports store.py. Q: how does the pane read? A: cairn/devices/cairn/device.py _trouble_pane_data calls store.live() and keeps its existing row mapping; it no longer raises on a missing bus, but it still raises if store_root() is not a directory (an absent store must not read as zero troubles, Law 7). Q: web_server? A: listener.py builds the same list from store.live(). Q: counting_block? A: _ask_clears returns {'clears': store.clears(IDENTITY_PREFIX)}, keeping the shape pulse() consumes; the ask= injection point stays. Q: the CLI? A: `live` prints from store.live(); `clear` measures the hand as today, calls DiagnosticBase.clear_trouble via a TroubleShim (identity, by, what_changed), then TroubleShim().drain(), then reads the ticket's file to print '<id>: cleared by <by> — now <standing>' (top of store = still OPEN with awaiting; cleared/ = CLEARED); a clear for a trouble that is not live prints 'declined — not live' and exits 1. Q: what about verbs? A: remove live, clear and clears from TroubleDevice.declared_verbs and delete _handle_live, _handle_clear and _handle_clears once nothing calls them; run grep to confirm. Q: which proofs change? A: any existing proof that sends those verbs is a consumer and is updated in the same build (grep proofs/ for verb='live' / 'clears' / 'clear' with to trouble first, and list them in writes_to). Q: where is the new proof? A: cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_trouble_never_rides_the_bus.py.

THE STORE MOVES INTO A PUBLISHED TOOL, superseding the how's 'grow store.py in place' and assumption (b). Measured 2026-10-18 by the survey: encapsulation_breaches (inspector.py:3709) admits a reach into a device only when the target is a tool NESTED in the device whose charter says published_by_device: true and names the module, so cairn/devices/trouble/store.py at the device root is an into_device breach for its 5 outside importers today. So: `git mv cairn/devices/trouble/store.py cairn/devices/trouble/tools/store/store.py`, add empty __init__.py in tools/ and tools/store/, and write tools/store/intention+why.json on the precedent cairn/devices/db_domain/tools/client/intention+why.json (published_by_device true, public_interface exactly ['cairn.devices.trouble.tools.store.store'], runtime_role tool, owner none of its own). Rewrite every importer to the new dotted path: cairn/tools/base/transitions.py, cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py, cairn/tools/operator_inbox/probes/operator_inbox_matches_live_state.py, cairn/tools/base/probes/does_the_bounce_blame_the_right_party.py, cairn/tools/base/probes/does_the_mail_lane_get_worked.py, and trouble.py's re-export. Drop 'cairn.devices.trouble.store' from cairn/devices/trouble/intention+why.json public_interface. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.
decisions.step: unlisted: where the store tool lives

decisions.text: THE TOOL'S SURFACE. tools/store/store.py holds store_root(roots=None) (unchanged), LIVE_SUMMARY_KEYS, CLEARED_DIR, listing(folder) (TroubleDevice._listing's body moved whole: [] for an absent folder, the UNREADABLE row with 'unreadable': True, the OFF-TEMPLATE why), live(roots=None) (the LIVE_SUMMARY_KEYS rows of listing(store_root(roots)); an unreadable row keeps its 'unreadable': True; RAISES FileNotFoundError when store_root(roots) is not a directory, so no reader can render an absent store as zero troubles, Law 7) and clears(prefix='', roots=None) (the rows _handle_clears returns, over the top and cleared/). It never folds pending emissions (folding is the owner's write). Its only module-level import stays cairn.tools.base.address; clears imports cairn.tools.system_word.fold and cairn.tools.artifact.artifact inside the function. trouble.py imports LIVE_SUMMARY_KEYS, CLEARED_DIR and store_root from the tool and its _listing delegates to listing(). The light-door proof test_the_store_root_is_a_light_door.py follows the door: _STORE points at tools/store/store.py, _ALLOWED adds cairn.tools.system_word and cairn.tools.artifact, tooth 3 compares trouble.store_root with the tool's, tooth 4 reads the TOOL's charter public_interface; the new proof's the_tool_reaches_no_host tooth measures the stronger claim by running it. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.

THE CLI CLEARS THROUGH A ModuleRaiser('cli'), superseding D1's 'via a TroubleShim'. Measured in shim.py _source_dirs: the drain reads every log home EXCEPT trouble's own, so an emission from a TroubleShim would never fold. `clear` measures the hand with artifact.caller() as today, calls ModuleRaiser('cli').clear_trouble(identity, by=by, what_changed=what_changed) with the hand riding the emission's values the way DiagnosticBase.clear_trouble carries it, then TroubleShim().drain(), then finds its own emission in the drain's folded list: outcome 'declined' prints 'declined — not live' and exits 1; else it reads the ticket's file (top = still OPEN, print who is still awaited; cleared/ = CLEARED) and prints '<id>: cleared by <by> — now <standing>'. `live` runs TroubleShim().drain() first (the owner folding in its own process, as `drain` already does) and prints from the tool's live(); --json prints the rows. `drain` keeps its reach('trouble') pulse. None of the three dials a request to trouble. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.

THE THREE READERS take scratch roots. cairn/devices/cairn/device.py _trouble_pane_data reads store.live(self._roots) and keeps its row mapping; it no longer needs a bus; the tool's raise on an absent store propagates (BaseShim.active_page renders it as an absent pane). cairn/devices/web_server/listener.py gains _trouble_rows(roots=None) -> [{id, standing, why, count}] from store.live(roots), and _handle_ws_troubles sends _trouble_rows(); 'trouble' leaves connect_system's devices list. cairn/machines/counting_block/block.py _ask_clears(roots=None) returns {'body': {'clears': store.clears(IDENTITY_PREFIX, roots)}}, the shape pulse() reads, and pulse passes its roots through. The probe cairn/devices/cairn/probes/trouble_panel_surfaces_live_troubles.py stops needing a bus in its context. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'.

The new proof is cairn/devices/trouble/proofs/test_trouble_never_rides_the_bus.py, written red-first (8 of 8 teeth red 2026-10-18). ModuleRaiser is cairn.tools.base.diagnostic.ModuleRaiser (diagnostic.py:479), a DiagnosticBase whose clear_trouble(identity, *, by, what_changed) is at diagnostic.py:391; ModuleRaiser('<module>') emits as that module. IDENTITY_PREFIX is the existing constant cairn/machines/counting_block/block.py:64, value "who-writes-what-"; the reader passes it to store.clears (block.py:289). Measured 2026-10-18. CC's call, per Akien 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-12 'approved thru PROVED, fastest route'

Settled by measurement: the charter is built at cairn/devices/trouble/tools/store/intention+why.json and carries all four fields — published_by_device True, public_interface ['cairn.devices.trouble.tools.store.store'], runtime_role 'tool', owner 'None of its own — a tool has users (Law 6)'; the builder adapts nothing, it is already there.
